notes: Provider-neutral definitions of the core scripts as callable tools. tools/mych.py translates them into OpenAI, Anthropic, Gemini and OpenAI-compatible formats and executes calls as argument lists (never through a shell). Command tokens: a plain string is literal ('{python}' is the running interpreter); {skill, path} resolves to a file inside a skill; {repo} resolves to a file in the MYCH-HORIZON repository; {param} inserts one value; {option, param} inserts the option and value when the value is present; {flag, when} inserts the flag when the boolean is true; {spread} appends each string of an array.

tools.name: mych_detect_capabilities
tools.description: Inventory what the environment can do: platform, commands, Python modules, GPU, credential variable names (never values), installed skills, MCP server names and specialist readiness. Read-only.

deep.description: Also run version commands and list global npm packages.

network.description: Probe a few public hosts over HTTPS.

tools.name: mych_scan_project
tools.description: Summarize a project folder for discovery: languages, frameworks, likely test and build commands, CI, docs, decision records, task ledgers; secret and data files are listed but never opened. Read-only.

path.description: Project folder to scan, relative to the workspace.

tools.name: mych_task_ledger
tools.description: Operate the project's task ledger, which enforces dependencies, approval gates and evidence before a task counts as verified. Commands that change state write only the ledger file.

file.description: Ledger path relative to the workspace (default .mych/tasks.json).

arguments.description: Remaining command-line arguments, for example ["T1", "--evidence", "pytest: 12 passed"].

tools.name: mych_validate_skill
tools.description: Validate a skill folder against the Agent Skills format and, for MYCH-HORIZON skills, their required layout and sections. Read-only.

path.description: Skill folder relative to the workspace.

tools.name: mych_route
tools.description: Suggest tier, disciplines, workflow and domain specialists for a task description. Heuristic: the coordinator confirms with the orientation questions. Read-only.
